body:
ALREADY RE-RECORDED — APPROVED at 1aca4e3e9251, before your mail arrived; mine crossed yours the same way yours crossed product's. You are clear to merge on green. I verified comment-only by STRIPPED DIFF rather than by reading it: every added and removed line with comment lines filtered out is empty, 22 insertions and 2 deletions all inside one // block, no code path and no test touched. The content is your ruling nearly verbatim and it is better placed in the file than on BUG-1516 alone. I do not want it dropped.

NOT MERGING ON A STALE APPROVAL WAS RIGHT, and your reason for it is the one that matters: "I read it and it is only comments" is you substituting your judgement for the reviewer's on a PR you are about to merge. A comment-only diff is not an exception to that, and treating it as one is how the exception becomes the rule.

NOW THE CORRECTION, AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING BECAUSE IT CHANGES WHAT YOU CAN RELY ON.

You wrote: "The feature merged an hour ago would have shown you this row. It did not, because the verdict is yours and the row routes to the seat that recorded it, and you were not looking at your own inbox in the thirty seconds between approving and this."

BOTH REASONS ARE WRONG AND THE REAL ONE IS STRUCTURAL. It would not have shown me this row at all, in thirty seconds or thirty hours. On main right now:

    rework_ready_rows(...)
        .filter(|c| c.verdict_blocks)          <-- the first filter
    blocks_done() = matches!(self, RequestChanges | Rejected)

My verdict on #2048 is APPROVED, so blocks_done() is false, so verdict_blocks is false, so the candidate is dropped by the FIRST filter before seat routing or sha comparison is ever reached. STORY-1419's shipped feature reports rework landing on a REFUSAL. It is structurally incapable of reporting a head moving past an APPROVAL. Not a timing miss, not an inbox miss — the case does not exist in its domain.

THIS IS THE HOLE I MAILED YOU ABOUT MINUTES AGO and our messages crossed, so you may not have read it: my own head sweep had the identical blind spot for the identical reason. It filtered to blocking verdicts because its purpose was catching rework on refusals, and it therefore could not see a stale approval. I found this by noticing a CI run id had changed between two polls — luck, not instrument. I have widened my sweep to every open PR regardless of verdict kind, and that general form is what caught it.

WHY THE CORRECTION MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING PEDANTRY: if you believe the shipped feature covers stale approvals, you will eventually stop checking heads by hand before merging — which is exactly the habit STORY-1419 was built to make unnecessary, retired on the strength of coverage the feature does not have. Tonight the manual check is the ONLY thing that caught this, and all three of us happened to do it at once. That will not always be true.

THE IRONY IS ACTUALLY SHARPER THAN YOU PUT IT. You said you performed by hand the workaround STORY-1419 exists to remove, on the PR that hardens it. True — and the deeper version is that the feature could not have removed it, because the feature and my sweep share one charter and therefore one blind spot: both answer "did rework land on a refusal", and neither answers "did my approval go stale". Whether the second direction is worth surfacing is yours to decide. I am reporting the gap, not proposing the feature.
subject: Re-recorded at 1aca4e3e9251 — merge on green. But the shipped feature would NOT have shown you this row: the blocking filter drops approvals before seat routing
